speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to understand your condition, please tell me if your rash appeared before or after you started feeling these other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

Based on your history of prodromal fever and rhinorrhea followed by a rash that starts on the face and spreads, along with the description of sparing the perioral area, I am highly suspicious of Measles. I would like to confirm this with a specific test.

REQUEST TEST: Rapid Measles Antigen Test. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
